kept.title: Remote Code Execution via Dynamic Import Injection
kept.description: The `mdcConfigs` template function generates code that performs dynamic imports using user-controlled `options.configs` array values, allowing an attacker to load arbitrary files or modules.
steps_to_exploit: Identify a way to influence `options.configs` through module configuration.
Inject a path to a malicious local or remote file (if supported by the environment).
Trigger the `getMdcConfigs()` function to execute the import.
kept.impact: Full system compromise via arbitrary code execution on the server.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution via Unsafe `evalInContext`
kept.description: The `evalInContext` utility and its usage in `MDCRenderer.vue` evaluate property strings without sufficient path validation, potentially allowing access to `__proto__` or other dangerous object prototypes.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a malicious component attribute string using `v-bind` or similar directives.
Include a path like `__proto__.toString` or other sensitive keys.
The application evaluates this against the `runtimeData` object.
kept.impact: Information disclosure or potential denial of service by modifying object prototypes.

kept.title: Arbitrary File Read via SSR/WASM Plugin configuration
kept.description: The `addWasmSupport` utility and build configuration allow arbitrary files ending in `.wasm` to be inlined, and `src/templates/mdc-highlighter.ts` reads files based on path parameters.
steps_to_exploit: Control the `shikiPath` variable during the module setup process.
Point the path to an sensitive system file that the process has permission to read.
The application will read and include the contents of this file in the build bundle.
kept.impact: Exposure of sensitive server files during the build process.

kept.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via `rehype-raw`
kept.description: The parser configuration enables `rehype-raw` with `allowDangerousHtml: true` and passes through arbitrary elements, failing to sanitize potential malicious script tags inside HTML blocks.
steps_to_exploit: Include raw HTML tags like `` within markdown content.
The `rehype-raw` plugin parses this into the AST.
The rendered output executes the payload in the user's browser.
kept.impact: Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the user's browser.

kept.title: Insecure `JSON.parse` of User-Controlled Input
kept.description: The highlighter event handler parses theme and options strings from query parameters directly using `JSON.parse` without validation.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a URL to `/api/_mdc/highlight` with a specially crafted JSON string in the `theme` query parameter.
The handler parses the input immediately, potentially crashing the server or exhausting resources.
While JSON.parse is not typically an execution vector, it can trigger massive object creation/CPU load.
kept.impact: Denial of service through malformed JSON input or resource exhaustion.

kept.title: Improper Validation of Link Protocols
kept.description: The `isAnchorLinkAllowed` function attempts to sanitize URIs but may be bypassed by various encoding tricks or path manipulations, allowing restricted protocols.
steps_to_exploit: Use obfuscated URI schemes or complex URL structures not caught by the `new URL()` constructor.
Target restricted protocols like `javascript:` or `vbscript:`.
The link is rendered as an `<a>` tag, allowing XSS upon user click.
kept.impact: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) when clicking malicious links.

kept.title: Information Leak via Default Export of Sensitive Configuration
kept.description: `build.config.ts` forces a `defineConfig` export that leaks the provided configuration object into the global scope in CommonJS environments.
steps_to_exploit: Access the `dist/config.cjs` file in a server environment where this config is loaded.
Inspect the exported `defineConfig` or the module exports to see the configuration details.

kept.title: Unsafe `eval`-like behavior in `evalInContext`
kept.description: The logic in `evalInContext` can traverse objects and potentially expose non-exported or internal properties based on input strings.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a custom component that binds attributes to `documentMeta` or other internal context objects.
The `reduce` function allows reaching into nested objects potentially outside intended scope.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to internal application state and data structures.

kept.title: Unbounded Regex Complexity in Highlighting
kept.description: The highlighter uses `oniguruma` or `javascript` regex engines to process code snippets, which are vulnerable to ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service) if crafted code inputs are provided.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a specially crafted, deeply nested code snippet as input to the markdown parser.
The Shiki highlighter attempts to tokenize the input, leading to catastrophic backtracking.
The server process becomes unresponsive.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) of the server rendering service.

kept.title: Insufficient Validation of `inlineCode` Attributes
kept.description: The `inlineCode` handler processes `attributes` directly and applies them to properties, allowing injection of arbitrary attributes (e.g., event handlers).
steps_to_exploit: Inject an attribute like `onmouseover=alert(1)` into the markdown code block syntax.
The handler assigns `node.attributes || {}` to the `properties` object.
The resulting HTML tag contains an event handler.

kept.title: Broken Access Control in `removeInvalidSnippets`
kept.description: The `removeInvalidSnippets` logic in `PageSnippet.vue` relies on `snippetParentNodes` to filter snippets, which could be bypassed by manipulating the AST structure or nested snippet requests.
steps_to_exploit: Create a malicious nested snippet that attempts to shadow or override parent snippet validation.
The recursive `removeInvalidSnippets` function might fail to account for the specific injection context of the parent.

kept.title: Insecure Component Resolution
kept.description: The `resolveComponentInstance` in `MDCRenderer.vue` resolves components globally, potentially allowing an attacker to render restricted internal components by name.
steps_to_exploit: Find the name of sensitive internal components.
Inject a component tag into the markdown, e.g., `<InternalAdminComponent />`.
The renderer attempts to resolve and render it.
kept.impact: Unauthorized component rendering potentially leading to UI spoofing or data leakage.

kept.title: Use of `unsafe-eval` by default
kept.description: The application relies on dynamic evaluation of string inputs within the `MDCRenderer` context for attribute binding, which violates CSP best practices and allows execution of unintended code.
steps_to_exploit: The system is architected to evaluate user-supplied strings as object accessors.
While primarily for data access, this design pattern is prone to injection when the input source is untrusted.
kept.impact: Weakened security posture and risk of code injection.

kept.title: Lack of Rate Limiting on Markdown API
kept.description: The `api/markdown.ts` endpoint and the `_mdc/highlight` handler do not implement rate limiting, allowing rapid-fire requests to consume server resources.
steps_to_exploit: Use an automated script to flood the server with markdown parsing requests.
The server spends significant CPU resources repeatedly parsing and highlighting.
Legitimate requests are denied due to server load.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via resource exhaustion.

kept.title: Dependency Risk: Use of Unmaintained/Vulnerable Plugins
kept.description: The project uses various markdown processing plugins that are frequently updated and have a large transitive dependency surface.
steps_to_exploit: Identify a known vulnerability in a transitive dependency (e.g., `unist`, `hast`, or `remark` plugins).
The application bundles these as part of its rendering pipeline.
kept.impact: Inheritance of vulnerabilities from the extensive dependency tree.
